speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your skin condition, can you describe the appearance, size, and duration of the lesions you are concerned about?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC). The combination of a non-healing, crusty lesion on a high-risk site (penis) and a similar lesion on a finger, in a 62-year-old male with a heavy smoking history and failed prior treatments, is highly suspicious for SCC. Given the potential for metastasis, I recommend a biopsy for histopathological confirmation.
